items.title: Ola's extra pay for faster rides feature doesn't work: CCPA asks it to scrap practice, slaps ₹10 lakh penalty
items.summary: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a penalty of ₹10 lakh on ANI Technologies Private Limited, which operates Ola, for misleading consumers into paying additional amounts to improve their chances of securing a ride. In an order dated November 10, the CCPA held that Ola's practice of prompting customers to pay extra before a driver accepted their booking amounted to a misleading advertisement, unfair trade practice and unfair contract under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. Hence, it ordered the platform to stop the feature/ practice while also imposing a penalty on it. The order was passed by Chief Commissioner Nidhi Khare and Commissioner Anupam Mishra . The proceedings arose from a complaint received in May 2025 concerning Ola's advance tipping feature. While customers waited for a driver to accept their booking, the app displayed messages suggesting that paying an additional amount could improve their chances of securing a ride. One such prompt stated: "Adding a tip might help increase the chances of getting a ride faster." items.title: Former YSRCP MP Vijayasai Reddy launches new party in Andhra Pradesh
items.summary: Former YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) MP V Vijayasai Reddy has returned to politics, launching the Parivarthana Rajaneethi Party (PRP) on Wednesday, November 11 at the A Convention Centre in Vijayawada. He said the party would challenge the dominance of two political families in Andhra Pradesh and create opportunities for younger leaders. Unveiling its white and saffron flag, featuring a Dharma Chakra at the centre, Vijayasai said the organisation would offer an alternative to the ruling Telugu Desam Party (TDP) and the Opposition YSRCP. Addressing the gathering, he said political leadership in the state should not remain confined to two families. He questioned why the Chief Minister, ministers and MLAs should come only from these families, referring to Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu and YSRCP president YS Jagan Mohan Reddy. He said people should have the freedom to question all political leaders, including himself, over wrongdoing. Vijayasai said the party would focus on identifying and nurturing young leaders rather than creating another individual political figure. He said he wanted a capable young person to become Chief Minister, regardless of caste or family background. Leader

items.title: Telangana to scrap intermediate colleges, bring class 11 and 12 under schools
items.summary: The Telangana government has announced that it will introduce a 10+2 grade education system in schools from the next academic year, effectively replacing the current system of treating the two years after matriculation as a separate ‘intermediate’ system. School education will be split into three main levels – primary (nursery to class 4), secondary education (classes 5 to 8), and senior secondary education (classes 9 to 12) – Chief Minister Revanth Reddy said on November 11 following a review meeting of the education department. Revanth Reddy also handles the education portfolio. The CM said that under the new system, students must be trained to have a command over language and communication skills by the time they complete class 12. He expressed concern over students discontinuing their education after class 10, with dropouts consisting predominantly of girls, and children from Dalit, tribal, and minority communities. He noted that dropout rates are significantly lower in government-run institutions such as Kendriya Vidyalayas, Navodaya Vidyalayas, and Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas, which offer continuous education up to class 12. items.title: Revanth Reddy inaugurates restored Thammidikunta Lake in Hyderabad
items.summary: Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy on Wednesday, November 11, inaugurated the restored Thammidikunta Lake in Hyderabad’s Madhapur, following the removal of encroachments and waste. He also said Phase I of the Musi River rejuvenation project would begin soon, seeking support for the government’s plans. The lake, restored by the Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA), has been expanded to around 30 acres. More than 30,000 truckloads of silt, construction debris, plastic and other waste, including biomedical waste, were removed during the work. Its depth has increased from 0.6 metres to 4.6 metres, while its water storage capacity has risen eightfold to 370 million litres, according to HYDRAA Commissioner A V Ranganath. The restored lake has a 1.6-km walking track, an open gym, a children’s play area, landscaped gardens and seating facilities. HYDRAA also reconstructed three inlets and an outlet to improve rainwater flow and diverted sewage through a 1,200-mm pipeline to prevent wastewater from entering the lake. items.title: Calcutta High Court dismisses NGO's plea for enquiry into demolition of its book stall during Durga Puja
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court on Tuesday dismissed Association for Protection of Democratic Rights' (APDR's) plea seeking an impartial, time-bound enquiry into identifying and holding accountable the persons responsible for the demolition of their temporary book stall near Jadavpur 8B Bus Stand without any prior notice during Durga Puja [Association for Protection of Democratic Rights v. The State of West Bengal and Ors.]. Justice Rishad Medora dismissed the plea on the ground that since the book stall was erected without the appropriate permission, no fundamental right of the petitioner (ADPR) was infringed. However, he noted that that ADPR was free to opt for any other remedy it deemed appropriate in pursuit of its enquiry into the demolition of its stall. "It does not appear that any fundamental right of the petitioner has been violated for it to approach this Court in its writ jurisdiction. Since no affidavit has been called for, the allegations made in the writ petition are deemed not to have been admitted by the respondents. The petitioner will be at liberty to pursue other remedies, if any, available to it in respect of the aforesaid demolition. The writ petition stands dismissed

items.title: CM Vijay meets TVK MLAs, asks them to focus on public grievances
items.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay has warned two Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) legislators facing allegations of misconduct that action could follow if their conduct damages the party’s reputation. He also asked all party MLAs to avoid controversies and concentrate on public grievances. CM Vijay held a nearly three-hour meeting with TVK legislators at a resort near Mamallapuram in Chengalpattu district on Wednesday, November 11. The meeting was held six months after the party formed the government, following a series of controversies involving its elected representatives. The two legislators who CM Vijay met separately were Thuraiyur MLA and Deputy Speaker Ravishankar and Kallakurichi MLA Arul Vignesh. Ravishankar was recently filmed assaulting a person who had approached him with a complaint. Vignesh is accused of inappropriate behaviour towards Kallakurichi District Collector Padmaja. Sources told TNM that CM Vijay reprimanded both legislators and cautioned them that the party would take action if they brought disrepute to the government or TVK.
